title: TABLE 56 CHARACTER PROFICIENCIES - the class grid with the ninja weapon-only rule
audit_comment: OA round forty (capture p. 99): Table 56 - the character proficiencies grid, the initial proficiencies, the levels per added proficiency and the non-proficiency penalties by class, with the ninja weapon-only rule

banner.title: TABLE 56 CHARACTER PROFICIENCIES, printed capture p. 99 - the OA character proficiencies round
banner.provenance: pinned from the 2018 print capture (the settling authority), with the compressed-print capture giving a second independent read of the table - the Table 56 grid cross-checked cell-by-cell between the two passes (the table printing on capture p. 99 of the print pass; compressed p. 52); every printed cell agrees - zero contested cells. The grid pins as a table: the class rows 0 samurai, 1 shukenja, 2 sohei, 3 kensai, 4 o. barbarian, 5 bushi, 6 wu jen and 7 ninja riding the first column comment, three data columns - the initial number of proficiencies at 1st level (5, 6, 4, 3, 9, 4, 6, 2), the levels per added proficiency as the denominator of the printed 1/N notation (1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 2, 3) and the non-proficiency weapon penalty (2, 4, 2, 3, 2, 2, 5, 4). The column doctrines ride the comments: the initial-number reading (the number at 1st level), the 1/N reading (1/1 a proficiency each level, 1/4 four levels per proficiency, 1st level included when counting) and the penalty reading (the minus on to hit with a weapon not proficient in). The ninja rule pins as a bool - the ninja can only use his proficiencies for ninja weapons, the non-proficiency penalty applying only to ninja weapons, all other weapons taking the other class penalty. The table tag T56Data identifier-safe per the R639 lesson; the slot-system prose cross-references stay with R650

rules/oanwprof.h, prefix dhm (verified free), 33 inlines (12
consts, 21 bools, no tables): the four categories (Common,
Artisan, Court, Barbarian) with the only-barbarians rule and the
category learning environments, the no-required-study-times and
tools-and-guidance learning doctrine, the base-chance rules
(identical to the to-hit roll, never improving with level), the
+1-per-slot improvement from 2nd level, the no-limit rule and
the never-below-3 floor, the magical-only-if-known rule, the
Akimori calligraphy example (two slots, base 17, 16 at third, 14
at fourth), the optional +1/+2 player bonuses (strictly
optional), the success-and-failure doctrine with the always-roll

inauspicious all-fail rule, 50 vs 100 times the host's level).

minuses where the print prints pluses, and the Akimori
arithmetic (the chance falling as the modifier rises) reads
nonsense with genuine minuses - genuine pluses pinned per the
